draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kumbalangi! Kerala Tourism calls this island village India's first eco-tourism village. On some nights the backwaters here glow with sea sparkle, which locals call Kavaru.
draft.hungryLine: You're in Kochi's backwater country, so think fresh prawns, fish molly and Kochi's own Meen Molagitta Curry.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk into Kumbalangi to see the Chinese fishing nets, then head over to Aroor, the fishing village across the water.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit by the backwaters at dusk and watch the Chinese fishing nets go up and down.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Aroor-Kumbalam Bridge, right by these backwaters, is the second longest bridge in Kerala.

spots.name: Kumbalangi
spots.detail: 11 min walk · Chinese fishing nets and backwaters

spots.name: Aroor
spots.detail: 22 min walk · Fishing village and seafood export hub

tips.title: Plan around the festivals.
tips.body: The Cochin Carnival runs from 20 December to 2 January, and Onam falls between mid-August and mid-September.

tips.title: Buy toddy from a local.
tips.body: Adulterated toddy is common, so your best bet is someone who taps their own coconut trees.

story.title: A city of visitors
story.body: For about 600 years, Kochi has hosted Arabs, Chinese, Portuguese, Dutch, English and more. You can taste that mix in the food.

story.title: The carnival begins
story.body: The Cochin Carnival started as part of Portuguese New Year celebrations. It's now one of the biggest parties in India.

story.title: Nets and backwaters
story.body: Kumbalangi is an island village among the backwaters, about 12 km from Kochi city centre. It's famous for its Chinese fishing nets.

story.title: India's first eco-tourism village
story.body: Kerala Tourism names Kumbalangi as the first eco-tourism village in India. Next door, Aroor ships seafood out to the world.

story.title: Wait for the glow
story.body: Stay by the water after dark and look for Kavaru. Tell me if you see it sparkle.
